arxiv-1802-03417.title: Narrow artificial intelligence with machine learning for real time estimation of a mobile agent’s location using Hidden Markov Models
arxiv-1802-03417.creator: Cédric Beaulac and Fabrice Larribe
arxiv-1802-03417.description: Abstract We propose to use a supervised machine learning technique to track the location of a mobile agent in real time. Hidden Markov Models are used to build artificial intelligence that estimates the unknown position of a mobile target moving in a defined environment. This narrow artificial intelligence performs two distinct tasks.

arxiv-1910-00492.title: Angular Control of Anisotropy-Induced Bound States in the Continuum
arxiv-1910-00492.creator: Samyobrata Mukherjee, Jordi Gomis-Bresco, Pilar Pujol-Closa, David Artigas, Lluis Torner
arxiv-1910-00492.description: Abstract Radiation of leaky modes existing in anisotropic waveguides can be cancelled by destructive interference at special propagation directions relative to the optical axis orientation, resulting in fully bound states surrounded by radiative modes. Here we study the variation of the loci of such special directions in terms of the waveguide constitutive parameters.

arxiv-2103-13857.title: A novel W 1 , ∞ W^{1,\infty} approach to shape optimisation with Lipschitz domains
arxiv-2103-13857.creator: Klaus Deckelnick, Philip J. Herbert, Michael Hinze
arxiv-2103-13857.description: Abstract . This article introduces a novel method for the implementation of shape optimisation with Lipschitz domains. We propose to use the shape derivative to determine deformation fields which represent steepest descent directions of the shape functional in the W 1 , ∞ − W^{1,\infty}- topology.

arxiv-2105-03476.title: Determination of the speed of light from the longitudinal modes beat frequencies of an open-cavity helium-neon laser
arxiv-2105-03476.creator: Mohamad Taim, Nicholas Kuder
arxiv-2105-03476.description: Abstract We empirically determined the speed of light by measuring the variation in longitudinal mode frequencies, or the beat frequencies, of an adjustable-length, open-cavity helium-neon laser as a function of its cavity length. The TEM 00 mode lasing output of the laser was analyzed using a fast frequency photodiode detector and a radio frequency spectrum analyzer.

arxiv-2305-17655.title: Understanding Blockchain Governance: Analyzing Decentralized Voting to Amend DeFi Smart Contracts
arxiv-2305-17655.creator: Johnnatan Messias, Vabuk Pahari, Balakrishnan Chandrasekaran, Krishna P. Gummadi, Patrick Loiseau
arxiv-2305-17655.description: Abstract . Smart contracts are contractual agreements between participants of a blockchain, who cannot implicitly trust one another. They are software programs that run on top of a blockchain, and we may need to change them from time to time (e.g., to fix bugs or address new use cases).

arxiv-2308-02616.title: Designing for Passengers’ Information Needs on Fellow Travelers: A Comparison of Day and Night Rides in Shared Automated Vehicles
arxiv-2308-02616.creator: Lukas A. Flohr, Martina Schuß, Dieter P. Wallach, Antonio Krüger, Andreas Riener
arxiv-2308-02616.description: Abstract Shared automated mobility-on-demand promises efficient, sustainable, and flexible transportation. Nevertheless, security concerns, resilience, and their mutual influence – especially at night – will likely be the most critical barriers to public adoption since passengers have to share rides with strangers without a human driver on board.

arxiv-2503-02550.title: SpecInF: Exploiting Idle GPU Resources in Distributed DL Training via Speculative Inference Filling
arxiv-2503-02550.creator: Cunchi Lv, Xiao Shi, Dong Liang, Wenting Tan, Xiaofang Zhao
arxiv-2503-02550.description: Abstract Deep Learning (DL), especially with Large Language Models (LLMs), brings benefits to various areas. However, DL training systems usually yield prominent idling GPU resources due to many factors, such as resource allocation and collective communication. To improve GPU utilization, we present SpecInF, which adopts a Spec ulative In ference F illing method to exploit idle GPU resources.

arxiv-2505-10313.title: Sensing a magnetic rare-earth surface alloy by proximity effect with an open-shell nanographene
arxiv-2505-10313.creator: Nicolò Bassi, Jan Wilhelm, Nils Krane, Feifei Xiang, Patrícia Čmelová, Elia Turco, Pierluigi Gargiani, Carlo A. Pignedoli, Michal Juríček, Roman Fasel, Richard Korytár, Pascal Ruffieux
arxiv-2505-10313.description: Abstract keywords Open-shell molecules, spin, phenalenyl,rare-earth surface, proximity interaction, scanning tunneling microscopy, XMCD 1 Abstract Open-shell nanographenes have attracted significant attention due to their structurally tunable spin ground state. While most characterization has been conducted on weakly-interacting substrates such as noble metals, the influence of magnetic surfaces remains largely unexplored.

arxiv-2509-17587.creator: Saveliy V. Skresanov
arxiv-2509-17587.description: Abstract An element x x of a group G G is a commutator if it can be expressed in the form x = a − 1 ​ b − 1 ​ a ​ b x=a^{-1}b^{-1}ab for some a , b ∈ G a,b\in G .

arxiv-2601-06087.title: The AI Roles Continuum: Blurring the Boundary Between Research and Engineering
arxiv-2601-06087.creator: Deepak Babu Piskala
arxiv-2601-06087.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Deepak Babu Piskala. The rapid scaling of deep neural networks and large language models has collapsed the once-clear divide between “research” and “engineering” in AI organizations. Drawing on public job descriptions, hiring loops, and org narratives from leading labs and tech companies, we propose the AI Roles Continuum : a spectrum in which Research Scientists, Research Engineers, Applied Scientists and Machine Learning Engineers share overlapping mandates.

pmc-10522719.title: Long-term treatment outcomes of temozolomide-based chemoradiation in patients with adult-type diffuse IDH-mutant grade 2 astrocytoma
pmc-10522719.creator: Giuseppe Minniti, Sergio Paolini, Manila Antonelli, Francesca Gianno, Paolo Tini, Gaetano Lanzetta, Antonella Arcella, Raffaella De Pietro, Martina Giraffa, Luca Capone, Andrea Romano, Alessandro Bozzao, Vincenzo Esposito
pmc-10522719.description: PurposeTo report the long-term outcomes in adult patients with grade 2 IDH-mutant astrocytoma treated with temozolomide (TMZ)-based chemoradiation. Methods: One hundred and three patients with histologically proven grade 2 astrocytoma received radiation therapy (RT), 50.4–54 Gy in 1.8 Gy fractions, and adjuvant TMZ up to 12 cycles.

pmc-10660987.title: A qualitative exploration of the facility-based trauma care for Road Traffic Crash patients in Bangladesh: When only numbers do not tell the whole story
pmc-10660987.creator: Samiun Nazrin Bente Kamal Tune, Amber Mehmood, Nahitun Naher, Bushra Zarin Islam, Syed Masud Ahmed
pmc-10660987.description: ObjectiveBangladesh is currently undergoing an epidemic of road traffic crashes (RTCs). In addition to morbidity and mortality, the economic loss from RTC as per cent of gross domestic product is comparatively higher than in countries with similar socioeconomic conditions. However, trauma care remained poorly developed as a specialty and service delivery mechanism.

pmc-11439047.title: Structural insights into the human P2X1 receptor and ligand interactions
pmc-11439047.creator: Felix M. Bennetts, Hariprasad Venugopal, Alisa Glukhova, Jesse I. Mobbs, Sabatino Ventura, David M. Thal
pmc-11439047.description: The P2X1 receptor is a trimeric ligand-gated ion channel that plays an important role in urogenital and immune functions, offering the potential for new drug treatments. However, progress in this area has been hindered by limited structural information and a lack of well-characterised tool compounds.

pmc-11680197.title: Receptor Binding Domain-Specific B Cell Memory Responses Among Individuals Vaccinated Against SARS-CoV-2
pmc-11680197.creator: Atharv Athavale, Anmol Gaur, Nafees Ahmed, Adarsh Subramaniam, Jyotsna Dandotiya, Sneha Raj, Santosh Kumar Upadhyay, Sweety Samal, Anil Kumar Pandey, Ramesh Chandra Rai, Amit Awasthi
pmc-11680197.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: The COVID-19 pandemic prompted unprecedented vaccine development efforts against SARS-CoV-2. India, which was one of the countries most impacted by COVID-19, developed its indigenous vaccine in addition to utilizing the ones developed by other countries. While antibody levels and neutralizing antibody titres are considered initial correlates of immune protection, long-term protection from the pathogen relies on memory B and T cells and their recall responses. In this regard, global research has primarily focused on mRNA-based vaccines.

pmc-12603560.title: Genomic Crosstalk Between Nuclear Receptors in Hormone-dependent Cancers
pmc-12603560.creator: Moray J Campbell
pmc-12603560.description: Nuclear receptors (NRs) orchestrate transcriptional programs that regulate cell fate decisions, and when these processes are disrupted, they can drive hormone-dependent cancers. This review summarizes mechanisms by which NRs function collectively, or crosstalk, to bring about the complex transcriptional control of cell fate decisions and indicate where these processes can act as cancer drivers.

pmc-13276749.title: A stereo dataset of annotated budgerigar flight trajectories for multi-agent collision avoidance studies
pmc-13276749.creator: SM Tawhid, Abdul Kader Mohim, Sk Shahed Ali, Kazi Tanzizul Haque Tanzil, Dip Nandi, Abhijit Bhowmik, Debajyoti Karmaker
pmc-13276749.description: This article presents a collection of 360 synchronized stereo video pairs capturing the flight behaviour of Budgerigars (Melopsittacus undulatus) in a controlled indoor arena. The recordings were acquired at 120 frames per second using a calibrated stereo camera setup with a fixed baseline.

pmc-13344866.title: Fear and picky eating‐related ARFID behaviors in children with food allergy
pmc-13344866.creator: Merve Karaca Şahin, Nilay Çalışkan, Hasan Tunç Şarman, Çağla Öztürk Turan, Güler Yıldırım, Eren Güzeloğlu, Hilal Güngör, Aslı Berivan Topçak, Hamit Boloğur, Şule Papağan, Ömer Yılmaz Ulutaş, Muhammed Fatih Erbay, Şefika İlknur Kökcü Karadağ, Deniz Özçeker
pmc-13344866.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundFood allergy is a chronic condition with psychosocial consequences for both children and their families. Strict elimination diets and fear of adverse reactions may contribute to maladaptive coping including behaviors avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID)‐related eating patterns.

pmc-13568431.title: Compressive Deformation, Damage Evolution, and Energy Absorption of 3D-Printed PLA and Short-Carbon-Fiber-Reinforced PLA Auxetic Metamaterials
pmc-13568431.creator: Lan Luo, Shidian Qiu, Maokai Li, Lianchao Wang, Zhengxian Liu
pmc-13568431.description: Auxetic mechanical metamaterials convert axial compression into lateral contraction, providing deformation modes that are attractive for lightweight energy absorbers. Here, fused deposition modeling was used to fabricate polylactic acid (PLA) and 10 wt% short-carbon-fiber-reinforced PLA (CF/PLA) auxetic metamaterials with arrow, re-entrant hexagonal, star-shaped, and chiral rotating topologies.

pmc-13583065.title: Large language model prompt engineering for medical education: A practical guide for the Australian and New Zealand College of Anaesthetists Final Examination
pmc-13583065.creator: Timothy J Trewren, Galina Gheihman, Kelly Bratkovic, D-Yin Lin, Stewart Anderson, Dario Winterton, Christina Gao, Brandon Stretton
pmc-13583065.description: Large language models (LLMs) can achieve passing scores in specialist-level examinations, yet their capacity to author high-stakes examination content remains under-explored. Compared with published human benchmarks, LLMs create questions roughly 10 times faster, and contextual memory across sessions enables rapid diversification of topic coverage. Prompt design therefore emerges as an academic, not merely technical, craft.
